findings.title: currency and status are interpolated into HTML without escaping
findings.explanation: Only `org_name` goes through `escapeHtml`. `invoice.currency` (`.toUpperCase()` does not escape anything) and `invoice.status` are inserted raw. They are probably constrained values today, but a schema change or a bad data import would turn this into stored XSS on an authenticated origin. Escape every interpolated value, or use a small template helper that escapes by default.

findings.title: toISOString() on period dates can shift the day
findings.explanation: If `period_start` and `period_end` are `DATE` columns, node-pg parses them as local-time `Date` objects. `toISOString()` converts to UTC, so on a server not running in UTC the printed date can be off by one day. That is a bad bug on an accounting document. Either cast in SQL (`to_char(i.period_start, 'YYYY-MM-DD')` or `i.period_start::text`) or confirm the column type and the server timezone.

findings.title: Amount formatting assumes 2-decimal minor units
findings.explanation: Dividing by 100 is wrong for zero-decimal currencies (JPY) and three-decimal currencies (KWD, BHD). The output has no thousands separators or currency symbol either. Use `Intl.NumberFormat` with the currency code and a per-currency minor-unit exponent, or reuse any existing money formatter in the codebase.

findings.title: Non-numeric invoiceId produces a 500 instead of a 404
findings.explanation: `Number('abc')` is `NaN`, which pg sends to an integer column and fails with an invalid-input error. The caller gets a 500 and the error is logged as a server fault. Validate the param (`Number.isInteger(id)`) and return 404 or 400. If the existing `/:invoiceId` route does the same, fix both or share a parser.

findings.title: Async handler has no error handling
findings.explanation: If `pool.query` rejects, Express 4 will not catch the rejection from an async handler, so the request can hang and trigger an unhandled rejection. Wrap the handler in try/catch or the project's async wrapper, unless the app already uses Express 5 or `express-async-errors`.

findings.title: Sensitive financial page lacks cache and security headers
findings.explanation: The response contains billing data but sets no `Cache-Control: private, no-store`, so shared proxies or browsers on shared machines may cache it. Consider also `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a restrictive CSP (`default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'`) as defense in depth for a server-generated HTML page.

findings.title: No tests
findings.explanation: There are no tests for this route. At minimum cover: successful render, 404 for another organization's invoice (the tenant-isolation guarantee the description relies on), 404 for an unknown id, a non-numeric id, and HTML escaping of an organization name such as `<script>`.

findings.title: HTML is minimal and not really print-ready
findings.explanation: The document has no `<html>`, `<head>`, `<title>`, `<meta charset>`, or `lang`, and no print styles. The customer wants something to hand to accounting, so add a basic structure, a title such as `Invoice #id`, and simple CSS. Consider labeling the document 'Invoice' consistently with the amount-due wording, since paid invoices would also read 'Amount due'.

findings.title: Query duplicates the existing invoice lookup
findings.explanation: The org-scoped lookup is nearly the same as the `/:invoiceId` handler. Extract a shared `getInvoiceForOrg(id, orgId)` helper so the tenant-scoping logic lives in one place and cannot drift between routes.

findings.title: escapeHtml is a local, hand-rolled helper
findings.explanation: HTML escaping is likely useful elsewhere. Move it to a shared util (or use an existing library or template engine that escapes by default) instead of defining it at the bottom of a route file. The inline object literal is also recreated on every character replacement; hoist it to a constant.

Review this pull request. ## Add printable invoice download Customers want a printable copy of an invoice for their accounting team. Adds `GET /invoices/:invoiceId/print`, which returns a simple HTML invoice. Scoped to the caller's organization like the other invoice routes. ## Diff ```diff diff --git a/src/routes/invoices.ts b/src/routes/invoices.ts index 938fffd..04598f2 100644 --- a/src/routes/invoices.ts +++ b/src/routes/invoices.ts @@ -39,3 +39,25 @@ invoicesRouter.get('/:invoiceId', async (req, res) => { if (!rows[0]) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' }) res.json(serializeInvoice(rows[0])) }) + +invoicesRouter.get('/:invoiceId/print', async (req, res) => { + const { rows } = await pool.query( + `SELECT i.id, i.amount, i.currency, i.status, i.period_start, i.period_end, o.name AS org_name + FROM invoices i JOIN organizations o ON o.id = i.org_id + WHERE i.id = $1 AND i.org_id = $2`, + [Number(req.params.invoiceId), req.user.orgId], + ) + const invoice = rows[0] + if (!invoice) return res.status(404).json({ error: 'not_found' }) + const amount = (Number(invoice.amount) / 100).toFixed(2) + res.type('html').send(` +

Invoice #${invoice.id}

+

${escapeHtml(invoice.org_name)}

+

Period: ${invoice.period_start.toISOString().slice(0, 10)} to ${invoice.period_end.toISOString().slice(0, 10)}

+

Amount due: ${amount} ${invoice.currency.toUpperCase()}

+

Status: ${invoice.status}

`) +}) + +function escapeHtml(value: string): string { + return value.replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => ({ '&': '&', '<': '<', '>': '>', '"': '"', "'": ''' })[c] as string) +} ``` Report every problem you would raise in a code review, from blocking issues to nits. Respond with only a JSON object, no prose before or after it: {"findings": [{"file": "path/to/file", "line": , "severity": "blocking" | "non-blocking" | "nit", "title": "", "explanation": ""}]} Use an empty findings list if you would approve the pull request as it is. Write the review in English.
